name: Should I replace the tub with a shower in my small bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Should I replace the tub with a shower in my small bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A shower-only conversion can free floor area and simplify access, but it is not automatically the best choice for every household. Removing the only tub may reduce flexibility for bathing children or affect future buyers, while a compact tub can preserve those uses at the cost of space.

Elite Remodeling & Design can compare fixture arrangements within the room’s actual dimensions and intended use. The decision should reflect who uses the bathroom, whether another tub exists, and how much entry clearance is available.

Key factors:
- Household bathing needs
- Number and location of other tubs
- Shower entry and door swing
- Storage and seating requirements

Decide whether the room is a primary, guest, or shared bathroom before selecting the fixture. Showers, tubs, valves, niches, and glass should be coordinated as one package rather than selected separately.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a shower when easier access and open floor area matter more than tub use. Keep a tub when it serves children, guests, or the household’s only tub. Compare the room’s entry clearance, storage, bathing needs, and other bathrooms before removing it.
